The wording in Q1's second paragraph may distinguish non-scheme money from money outside the combined scheme-money-and-Hong-Kong description. Does that distinction affect the reach of the continuing Schedule 11 expectations? It does not change the selected positive applicability antecedent.

citations.quote: The CMR will apply to an RA 13 licensed corporation (LC) and its associated entity (AE) in respect of “scheme money” received or held in Hong Kong by the RA 13 LC or its AE in the course of conducting Type 13 regulated activity by the RA 13 LC, regardless of the role played by such LC.

In such cases, the depositary is expected to observe relevant requirements under Schedule 11 to the Code of Conduct for Persons Licensed by or Registered with the Securities and Futures Commission (Schedule 11), in particular paragraphs 9 (relating to how subscription and redemption proceeds should be held) and 11 (relating to distribution proceeds).

readings.distinction: Considered three attachments: role independence within the stated RA13 conditions; restriction to transfer-agent activities because the question concerns that role; and displacement of the course-of-RA13 condition by the final modifier. Only the first is defensible in the complete answer: “regardless” excludes a role restriction, while the express course-of-activity condition remains. No rival predicate is retained merely to create diversity. The later Schedule 11 language preserves separate expectations where CMR does not apply; it does not qualify role independence or make Schedule 11 compliance a prerequisite.

in_hong_kong is defined for scheme money, so it cannot independently represent the location of non-scheme money when interpreting Q1's subsequent qualification.
